judge_assessment.explanation: Both hard failures are exact. Problems 1 through 5 each print 'Circle the way you picked: count on / double / near double / make ten' and verify.json ids 1-5 each carry a single eval of the sum -- and the answer key does name an intended choice per item ('best way: count on', 'best way: double', 'best way: make ten', 'count on from the larger part', 'near double'), so a gradeable response exists that verification never records. Problem 9 says 'Explain what he did wrong on the lines' and problem 10 says 'Show the order you chose, say which fast way it let you use'; both ids carry only an eval, and final_response.md states 'Nothing on this sheet is genuinely open-ended, so there is nothing flagged for manual review'. That is the false claim. The arithmetic is clean -- I get 9, 8, 10, 9, 9, 3, 4, 8, 8, 10 exactly as the judge did, plus study-guide try-its 8, 5, 10 -- so the REJECT rests solely on the trust boundary, which is where the rubric puts it.

strengths_to_preserve: The strategy selection is the pedagogical heart of the sheet and it is well built: 7+2 (tiny addend) invites count-on, 4+4 is a clean double, 6+4 is a ten-partner pair, 3+6 forces commuting to the larger addend before counting on, 4+5 is a near double. The facets alternate with a maximum same-facet run of 1 after the warm-up, which is what 'interleaved' is supposed to mean.

Problem 1's key entry says 'Accept also: a student who makes ten first (7 + 2 is one less than 7 + 3) still gets 9; the count-on is the shortest route.' An efficiency sheet that admits more than one efficient route, and says which is shortest and why, is teaching strategy rather than enforcing a single ritual. Preserve that framing -- it is also the reason the circled selection needs a manual entry rather than an exact-match check.

Problem 9's error is chosen precisely: Sam holds the larger part and then counts the held number as his first count. The key isolates the mistake to 'where he started counting', and the study guide's watch-out box states the same rule in the child's own words. The declared trap value 7 follows from that method, not from arbitrary arithmetic.
Problem 10 is a real synthesis item at this level: 2+3+5 can be reordered so that (2+3)+5 becomes 5+5, which is simultaneously a double and a ten-partner pair, and the key credits 2+(3+5) as well.

root_causes.description: The coverage contract is stated per PROBLEM, not per printed RESPONSE SLOT. SKILL.md's JSON-format section says verification 'hard-fails unless every problem id 1..N has at least one check', and verify.py enforces exactly that. One check therefore discharges a problem that prints two or three separate things for the student to write, and the gate chain reports the sheet as fully verified.
evidence: worksheet problems 1-5 each print 'Circle the way you picked: count on / double / near double / make ten' -- a selection response
verify.json ids 1-5 each hold exactly one eval entry covering only the sum
the answer key names an intended selection for each ('best way: count on', 'best way: double', 'best way: make ten', ...), so the selection has a gradeable key that verification never records
SKILL.md: 'every problem id 1..N has at least one check'

root_causes.description: SKILL.md actively steers error-analysis items away from 'manual': 'error-analysis ("find and fix the mistake") via the ordinary types --- the planted wrong result is checkably wrong and the correction checkably right. Reserve `manual` for genuinely open reasoning.' A find-and-fix item has TWO halves: the correction (checkable) and the diagnosis (not). The instruction covers only the first half, so the generator types the whole problem as eval/solve and the honest manual flag is never raised.
evidence: worksheet problem 9: 'Explain what he did wrong on the lines, then write the correct sum on the answer line.' -- verify.json id 9 is a lone eval (2+6 -> 8)
worksheet problem 10: 'Show the order you chose, say which fast way it let you use, then write the total.' -- verify.json id 10 is a lone eval (2+3+5 -> 10)
final_response.md: 'Nothing on this sheet is genuinely open-ended, so there is nothing flagged for manual review'

improvements.title: Every printed response slot needs its own verification entry, not one per problem
improvements.proposed_change: Change the coverage rule from 'one check per problem id' to 'one check per printed response slot'. Concretely: (a) rewrite the SKILL.md JSON-format sentence to require an entry for every blank, box or \ansblank the item prints, using a `manual` entry when a slot is a mark or a sentence; (b) have tests/check_layout.py count the response macros inside each \problem segment and fail when that count exceeds the number of verify entries carrying that id. The schema already supports several entries per id -- For this sheet, ids 1-5 each need a second entry recording the circled strategy -- a manual entry is the honest type here, because the key itself accepts more than one efficient route on problem 1.
improvements.regression_test: Add a fixture worksheet whose problem 1 prints two \ansblank slots with a verify JSON carrying a single entry for id 1, and assert check_layout.py exits non-zero naming problem 1. It passes (exit 0) today, which is the defect.
improvements.expected_impact: Restores coverage of the response the prompt centres on ('selecting an efficient strategy'). Today the sheet's headline skill is the only thing on the page that verification ignores.
improvements.risk: Medium. Counting response macros will initially fire on sheets that print a decorative underline, and on the 'Answer:' line that some templates emit in addition to an inline blank. Land the checker in warn-only mode for one run, tune against the existing eval corpus, then make it a hard gate.

improvements.title: Explanations and drawn/marked work must be declared manual, not folded into a numeric check
improvements.proposed_change: Amend SKILL.md so that a find-and-fix or error-analysis item is declared as TWO entries under one id: the ordinary typed check for the correction, plus a `manual` entry whose `desc` states the full-credit diagnosis. Extend the same rule to any stem containing 'explain', 'tell what ... did wrong', 'draw', 'cross out', 'circle', 'show your work' or 'write the equation'. Back it with a lint in tests/check_layout.py that scans problem prose for those verbs and fails when the matching id carries no `manual` entry. Problems 9 and 10 each need a manual entry alongside the eval: id 9's desc should state that full credit names WHERE Sam started counting, and id 10's should state that the child must show an order and name the strategy it enabled.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture: a worksheet whose problem 2 reads 'Explain what she did wrong, then write the correct answer' with a verify JSON holding only an eval entry for id 2. Assert the build exits non-zero (or exit 2 with problem 2 listed as manual). Today the chain exits 0 and the delivery text claims '0 manual'.
improvements.expected_impact: Both open items become visible as exit-2 manual review, and the delivery text stops claiming zero manual on a sheet with two written-explanation slots.
improvements.risk: Medium: a verb lint over prose will produce false positives (a stem that says 'draw' inside a worked hint). Ship it as exit-2 manual visibility rather than exit-1, which is the honest outcome anyway and cannot block a correct build.

case_summary: Pedagogically this is the strongest sheet in my shard: three named strategies, a two-problem warm-up, then genuine interleaving where the method choice is the work, an error-analysis item whose planted mistake is the exact off-by-one that count-on produces, and a three-addend synthesis challenge that pays off the ten-partner idea. All ten sums and all six study-guide results recompute correctly. It is rejected because verification covers only the numbers: the five circled strategy selections -- the thing the prompt actually asked the sheet to exercise -- and the two written explanations in problems 9 and 10 are all outside the verify data, while final_response.md declares the sheet has no open-ended item at all. Both root causes are in SKILL.md, not in this case.
